alert.title: Payment confirmations timing out right after the v2.6.3 release
alert.symptoms: Since about 12 minutes after the v2.6.3 Friday-afternoon release, payment confirmation calls are timing out and roughly 21% of checkout attempts fail; the API pods are up but requests queue for the database.
alert.error_message: HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms

response.root_cause: Likely database connection pool exhaustion introduced in the v2.6.3 release (e.g., increased query load or mis‑configured HikariCP max pool size), causing requests to queue and time out
response.blast_radius: Payments‑API service; impacts all checkout flows, currently ~21% of transactions fail, affecting revenue and user experience for all customers using the platform
first_actions: Review the v2.6.3 code diff for new or changed DB queries and HikariCP settings
Check database and HikariCP metrics (active connections, wait queue length, latency) to confirm pool saturation
If pool exhaustion is confirmed, either roll back v2.6.3 or increase the HikariCP max pool size and monitor the effect

New alert: Payment confirmations timing out right after the v2.6.3 release. Service: payments-api, severity: SEV1.
Symptoms: Since about 12 minutes after the v2.6.3 Friday-afternoon release, payment confirmation calls are timing out and roughly 21% of checkout attempts fail; the API pods are up but requests queue for the database.
Error: HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms

Evidence (only these incidents may be cited):
Incident INC-002 (payments-api, SEV1, 2026-05-15T14:32:10Z):
Symptoms: payments-api p99 latency above 4.8s and checkout error rate above 23% starting ~12 minutes after the v2.3.0 Friday deploy; new checkouts failing with DB connection errors.
Root cause: The v2.3.0 deploy's new order-confirmation retry path opens a DB session per retry without releasing it on timeout, exhausting the 20-connection Postgres pool within minutes of Friday peak traffic.
Resolver: Priya Nair

Incident INC-016 (order-worker, SEV1, 2026-07-21T17:03:26Z):
Symptoms: order-worker pods repeatedly OOMKilled every 20-30 minutes since a deploy 2 hours ago; job processing throughput down 60%.
Root cause: A newly upgraded image-resize library (v4.2.0) leaks native memory buffers on each thumbnail generation call, growing pod RSS until the kubelet OOM-kills the container.
Resolver: David Kim

Incident INC-009 (payments-api, SEV1, 2026-06-19T15:10:47Z):
Symptoms: Same signature as INC-002: p99 latency above 4.6s and checkout errors above 20% about 15 minutes after the v2.3.1 Friday deploy.
Root cause: Same order-confirmation retry session leak as INC-002 (still unfixed in code), triggered again by Friday deploy traffic.
Resolver: Priya Nair

Incident INC-012 (auth-service, SEV1, 2026-07-01T03:27:54Z):
Symptoms: 100% of login and token-refresh requests failing with SSL handshake errors starting at 03:27 UTC.
Root cause: The TLS certificate for auth.shipfast.example expired; cert-manager's renewal job had been silently failing for 3 weeks due to an expired DNS-01 challenge API token.
Resolver: Emily Chen
